## Structural orientation: Zed editor

**Workspace, not a single crate.** The root `Cargo.toml` defines a Cargo workspace with **236 member crates** under `crates/`, plus `extensions/` (bundled extensions), `assets/`, `docs/`, `tooling/`, `ci/`, `script/`. Total ~3,750 source files, ~54.5k symbols, ~73MB of crate source (excluding `target/`). This is the Zed code editor.

**Main architectural pieces**, based on import fan-out/fan-in and directory structure:

- **GPUI (`crates/gpui`)** — the custom UI/app framework underlying everything (highest fan-in of any internal crate: 1,017 imports across the workspace). Has platform backends split out: `gpui_macos`, `gpui_linux`, `gpui_windows`, `gpui_web`, `gpui_wgpu`, `gpui_tokio`, `gpui_platform`.
- **Editor core**: `editor` (highest internal fan-out, 71 imports — the central text-editing component), backed by `text`, `rope`, `multi_buffer`, `buffer_diff`, `sum_tree` (the rope/CRDT-like data structures), and `language`/`language_core`/`languages` (syntax, LSP-aware language support) plus `lsp` itself.
- **Project/workspace layer**: `project`, `worktree`, `workspace`, `fs`, `settings`/`settings_content` — file system, project model, multi-pane workspace shell.
- **Collaboration**: `client`, `rpc`, `proto`, `collab` (server), `channel`, `call`, `livekit_client`/`livekit_api` — real-time collab infrastructure.
- **AI/agent layer** — a large and clearly actively-developed area: `agent`, `agent_ui` (43 imports out, one of the biggest consumers), `agent_servers`, `acp_thread`, `context_server`, `edit_prediction` + `edit_prediction_context`/`edit_prediction_cli`/`edit_prediction_metrics`/`edit_prediction_ui`, `language_model`/`language_models`/`language_models_cloud`, plus per-provider crates: `anthropic`, `open_ai`, `google_ai`, `bedrock`, `mistral`, `deepseek`, `copilot`/`copilot_chat`, `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `codestral`, `open_router`, `x_ai`, `opencode`.
- **Debugging**: `dap`, `dap_adapters`, `debugger_ui`, `debugger_tools`.
- **Extensions system**: `extension`, `extension_api`, `extension_host`, `extension_cli`, `theme_extension`, `debug_adapter_extension`, `language_extension`, plus the top-level `extensions/` directory of bundled extension sources.
- **UI toolkit**: `ui`, `ui_macros`, `ui_input`, `component`, `component_preview`, `icons`, `theme`/`theme_settings`/`theme_selector`, `title_bar`/`platform_title_bar`.
- **Terminal**: `terminal`, `terminal_view`.
- **Vim emulation**: `vim`, `vim_mode_setting`.
- **App shell / entry point**: `zed` crate (`crates/zed/src/zed.rs`) ties everything together; `crates/zed/src/visual_test_runner.rs` is a notable high-fan-out file used for UI tests.
- **Supporting infra**: `db`/`sqlez`/`sqlez_macros` (persistence), `settings`/`settings_macros`/`settings_json`, `telemetry`/`telemetry_events`, `auto_update`, `zlog` (logging), `collections`, `util`/`util_macros`.

The dependency shape (GPUI and `collections`/`std`/`anyhow`/`futures` as near-universal leaves, `editor`/`agent_ui`/`project`/`workspace` as high-fan-out hubs) matches a layered architecture: GPUI framework → core data/text structures → editor/project/workspace domain logic → feature crates (agent, debugger, vim, extensions) → the `zed` binary that composes them.
